Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testJira567` in `ArrayUtilsAddTest` is testing the `ArrayUtils.addAll` method from Apache Commons Lang library. The test first attempts to add an `Integer` array and a `Long` array successfully, which is a valid operation. However, the test then tries to add an `Integer` array and a `Long` array again, which should result in an `IllegalArgumentException` because it is not allowed to store a `Long` in an `Integer` array. The test expects this exception and catches it as expected.

The current bug report highlights an issue with `ArrayUtils.addAll` when handling mixed array types. The reported stack trace shows that when trying to add an `Integer` array and a `Long` array together, an `ArrayStoreException` is thrown inside the `ArrayUtils.addAll` method.

Upon inspection of the code snippet of the failing test, we can see that the failing scenario matches the reported issue. The test is indeed trying to combine arrays of incompatible types without proper handling, leading to an exception being thrown.

To localize the fault, we should look into the implementation of the `ArrayUtils.addAll` method in Apache Commons Lang to understand why it fails to handle mixed array types properly.

I will now proceed to investigate the `ArrayUtils.addAll` method to identify the root cause of the failure.
